chunks.title: Standard Bank Group (Standard Bank) COP31 Role & Commitments
chunks.text: Standard Bank Group is a Global Commercial Bank headquartered in South Africa. At UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya (November 9-20, 2026), its verified role is: COP31 Business Forum Climate Finance & Investments Working Group member. Verified COP31 2026 climate finance commitment: ZAR 250–300B+ sustainable finance mobilization across African renewable energy, climate resilience & urban infrastructure. Source verification: https://www.copbusiness.org/papers/COP31_WG_climate-finance-investments.pdf.

chunks.title: Standard Bank Financing Instruments & Ticket Bounds
chunks.text: Standard Bank Group provides the following climate financing instruments: Green Loan, Sustainability-Linked Loan, Renewable Project Finance, Blended Adaptation Finance. Typical transaction ticket range is USD 5,000,000 to USD 250,000,000. Eligible applicant profiles include: Large Corporate, Project SPV, Municipality, Financial Intermediary.

chunks.title: Standard Bank Priority Climate Sectors & Regional Mandate
chunks.text: Priority climate sectors funded by Standard Bank Group: Renewable Energy, Electrification & Grid, Climate Adaptation & Resilience, Sustainable Agriculture & Water, Resilient Cities & Infrastructure. Target geographic focus includes: Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, South Africa, Kenya. Projects outside primary regions or ticket bounds may require syndicated or on-lending structures.

chunks.title: Standard Bank Mandatory Form & Underwriting Requirements
chunks.text: Mandatory requirements to complete Standard Bank's application form: African operating presence & Equator Principles screening; Standard Bank Sustainable Finance Framework alignment; Bankable cash flows or DFI partial risk guarantee. Explicit exclusion rules: New coal-fired power plants. Official application portal: https://www.standardbank.com/sbg/standard-bank-group/about-us/sustainability.

chunks.title: Standard Bank Form Template: Global Corporate & Investment Bank Green / Sustainability-Linked Finance Mandate Intake
chunks.text: Standard Bank Group uses the 'Global Corporate & Investment Bank Green / Sustainability-Linked Finance Mandate Intake' workflow governed by LMA/APLMA Green Loan Principles (GLP), Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles (SLLP) & ICMA GBP. Typical review timeline is 3–8 weeks (Sustainable Finance Structuring -> Credit Committee -> Syndication/Close). Form sections required: 1. Borrower Overview, 2. Structuring, 3. Transition Credibility, 4. Risk & Underwriting, 5. Mandate Pitch.

chunks.title: Standard Bank Guidance for 'Corporate Borrower & Operating Jurisdiction'
